title: EON Stream module manifest (v0 — UNSTABLE)
description: Describes a EON Stream module: what it is, what it needs, what it is allowed to do, and who signed it. v0 is explicitly unstable and may break without a migration path. First-party modules use this same schema and the same permission model as third-party ones (madde 3).

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS schema the document is written against.

id.description: Globally unique, reverse-DNS. Immutable for the life of the module: it is the identity used by dependencies, signatures and revocation.

name.description: Human-readable name. Localisable via the i18n map (madde 40).

version.description: Semantic version of the module itself.

kind.description: What class of module this is. Determines which host surfaces it may attach to. A module declares exactly one kind.

api.description: Range of EON Stream module API versions this module works against. The client refuses to load a module whose range excludes its own API version, and says so (madde 5).

runtime.description: How the module is executed. 'declarative' carries no code at all and is the only runtime available in v1 for third-party modules (madde 4). 'wasm' is the intended sandbox for code-executing modules and is not implemented yet. 'native' is reserved for first-party modules compiled into the client.

entry.description: Entry point relative to the module root. A declarative module points at its JSON document; a wasm module at its .wasm binary. Must stay inside the module root -- the client creates that directory and joins this onto it.

permissions.description: Capabilities the module requests. Each maps to a host function the sandbox grants or withholds; nothing is granted implicitly. A declarative module may request nothing. Requests are shown to the user before installation.

permissionRationale.description: Per-permission justification shown to the user. A permission without a rationale is a review finding, not an error.

dependencies.description: Other modules required at runtime. If one is missing the client offers to install it; a material package that needs an absent viewer opens partially rather than not at all (madde 16c).

builds.description: Which build profiles may load this module. An Edu build loads only modules signed with the Edu key (madde 22); declaring 'edu' here is a statement of intent, not the enforcement — enforcement is the signature.

license.description: SPDX identifier for the module's own code or content.

icon.description: Path within the module, or a data: URI. A remote URL is rejected -- fetching one would tell its host that this module is installed. The pattern enforces it rather than leaving it to each implementation.

i18n.description: Locale overrides for name and description. Keys are BCP 47 tags.

signature.description: Detached signature envelope. Absent in source trees; required for anything the client installs. See docs/signing-and-revocation.md.

allOf.$comment: A theme carries no code, ever. This is the hard boundary in madde 4 — expressed in the schema so it cannot be forgotten in an implementation.

madde 4, generalised. A declarative module carries no code, so there is nothing that could call a granted host function: a permission request on one is a mistake or a disguise. The theme rule below is the stricter special case -- a theme must also be declarative in the first place.
